title: Day 22 — Minimum Meeting Rooms
prompt: Given meeting intervals, we need the minimum number of rooms. The planner is over-booking: back-to-back meetings that just touch are counted as conflicts. How would you fix it?

clarifications.answer: Intervals are [start, end) — end exclusive. A meeting ending at 10 and one starting at 10 do NOT conflict and can share a room.
Two meetings conflict if one starts strictly before the other ends. The answer is the peak number of simultaneously-active meetings.
The two-pointer sweep over sorted starts and ends is fine — the bug is only the comparison at the boundary.
Return the maximum concurrency — the most meetings active at any instant.

hints: Walk the touching case [[1,2],[2,3]] through the sweep by hand: how many rooms does it report, and how many should it?
With end-exclusive intervals, a start equal to an end is NOT an overlap.
Change the sweep comparison from 'starts[i] <= ends[j]' to 'starts[i] < ends[j]'.
